findings.title: Well-hoist assembly
findings.claim: The focus's language of Satanic distance can be rendered through a complete lifting assembly in which a tethered weight, raised fitting, cord, bucket, and handle make inaccessible provision receivable.
findings.mechanism: The nominated branches form one coherent well-hoist: distance supplies the well and tether, elevation supplies the raised fitting, and the bucket parts turn a hidden source into received provision. The image gives concrete mechanics to the pericope's movement from inaccessible source to knowledge, mercy, and gift.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can track the macro movement as a physical sequence of reaching, lifting, receiving, and carrying.
findings.containment: The complete assembly is a material analogy from the trusted channel nomination; it does not replace the focus's local warning about worship and Satan.

epistemic.reason: The complete assembly is a material analogy from the trusted channel nomination; it does not replace the focus's local warning about worship and Satan.

findings.title: Hidden agency behind the proxy

findings.containment: The hidden-agency reading is an inference from the coordinated negations and later Satan label; a simpler quality-only reading remains open.

findings.title: Kinship reconfiguration

findings.mechanism: Abraham's withdrawal from false worship is followed by gifts, mercy, descendants, and a brother. The warning stands at a hinge where inherited kinship is painfully limited but care-bearing kinship is reconfigured rather than abolished.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold moral separation and continued care together without reducing either to a simple rejection of family.
findings.containment: The later gifts and family relations ground reconfiguration; they do not establish that gifts are a transactional replacement for the father.

epistemic.reason: The later gifts and family relations ground reconfiguration; they do not establish that gifts are a transactional replacement for the father.

findings.title: External communal worship contact
findings.claim: The focus's prohibition of worship directed to Satan gains a concrete object contrast when the added 1:5 speaks in a first-person plural voice of worship directed to the addressed divine object.
findings.mechanism: The focus worship carrier at 19:44:3:1 is paired with the exact external worship occurrence at 1:5:2; the external act makes the focus's problem a redirection of worship, not worship as an undifferentiated act.
findings.reader_payoff: The contrast makes direction and object of worship easier to track across the macro overlay.
findings.containment: Phase 2 only: this is a bounded contact with 1:5, not an import of the surrounding passage or a replacement for the native sequence.

epistemic.reason: Phase 2 only: this is a bounded contact with 1:5, not an import of the surrounding passage or a replacement for the native sequence.

findings.title: External straight-path overlay
findings.claim: The external straight-path wording adds explicit orientation and lost-course danger to the focus's rival-route reading.
findings.mechanism: The focus worship carrier at 19:44:3:1 is paired with exact external path occurrences at 1:6 and 1:7; route language makes the focus's directional problem concrete without importing the external passage as a whole.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how a worship choice is also a question of route, orientation, and departure from the right course.
findings.containment: Phase 2 only: retain the exact path contact as a lean overlay and do not import external discourse without a specific focus delta.

epistemic.reason: Phase 2 only: retain the exact path contact as a lean overlay and do not import external discourse without a specific focus delta.
